found_by: the soak's fuzzer, round 5 of the first --fuzz soak (2026-09-05): UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, member access within misaligned address for struct ext4_xattr_list_entry, in ext4_xattr_list from ext4b_listxattr
base: a healthy 2 MiB volume from this driver's own format (ext4, 1 KiB blocks), one file with two extended attributes

edits.to: two, with names whose length plus NUL is not a multiple of eight

symptom: ext4_xattr_list lays each list entry -- a struct holding pointers -- directly after the previous entry's NUL-terminated name, so the second entry starts on an odd address. ARM64 tolerates the misaligned loads, which is why no mount ever crashed; it is undefined behaviour and UBSan reports it on any listxattr of an inode with two attributes. The fuzzer's own artifact was a corrupt 1.5 MB image; this crafted healthy volume shows the same report, which is the point: it is not a hostile-input bug.
fixed_by: patch 0079: the stride from one list entry to the next is padded to the entry's alignment, in the size pass and the fill pass alike
reproduce: make test-asan, or build/bin/ext4dump xattr /f on a sanitizer build # must print both names and no 'runtime error'
